title: Bhindi (Ladies Finger): modeled ₹888/qtl left, Palayam → Mannar
summary: February 2025: reported bhindi (Ladies Finger) prices at Palayam and Mannar imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 20 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹888 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 1,176 same-variety market pairs screened for bhindi (Ladies Finger) in February 2025; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Mannar report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: February 2025
scenes.caption: Palayam (Kerala) and Mannar (Kerala) both reported bhindi (Ladies Finger) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 20 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Palayam reported a median ₹3,000 per quintal. Mannar reported a median ₹4,250 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,200/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,200 per quintal, and Mannar was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 260 km by road
scenes.caption: 260 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~5 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹56/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹671 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹451 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Mannar report, the rule selects 20 of 20 modeled shipping days. 20 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹888 per quintal (₹658 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Bhindi (Ladies Finger) route from Palayam to Mannar was positive on 100% of matched days in February 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹88,800, or ₹65,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to bhindi (Ladies Finger)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹56/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Bhindi (Ladies Finger) route from Palayam to Mannar was positive on 100% of matched days in February 2025. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹88,800, or ₹65,800 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
